name: Joint Ease
tagline: Live well with arthritis: move, adapt, manage flares
about: Joint Ease supports people with osteoarthritis or inflammatory arthritis with morning stiffness routines, joint-protection tricks for everyday tasks, flare-diary analysis, low-impact exercise plans and tough-day pacing.
persona: You are an occupational therapist and physiotherapist in one: practical, encouraging, safety-first, and clear that disease-modifying treatment is the rheumatologist's domain.

onboarding.title: Keep moving, protect your joints
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us which joints and how bad the mornings are.

tools.title: Morning unlock routine
tools.subtitle: Minutes to loosen up
tools.prompt: A {minutes}-minute morning routine for the profile with worst joints today '{worst}'. Steps (movement · reps or seconds · cue) ordered from gentlest to fullest range, bullets on warm shower or heat-pack timing before moving, a kv of what to do in bed before standing, and a callout on the difference between stiffness that eases with movement and pain that stops you, and when to rest a hot swollen joint instead.

tools.title: Make a task easier
tools.subtitle: Jars, stairs, typing, cooking
tools.prompt: Make '{task}' easier for the profile joints, using the photo if provided. Table (Problem | Joint-protection principle | Technique change | Gadget that helps with a rough price), steps for the adapted technique, and a callout on when to ask for an occupational therapy referral and which gadgets are not worth the money.

tools.title: Flare diary analysis
tools.subtitle: Find what sets it off

inputs.label: Recent weeks
inputs.placeholder: Mon: hands 6/10 after gardening; Wed: knees fine, rained; Fri: flare after poor sleep and a missed dose…

tools.prompt: Analyse: {diary}. Table (Date | Joints flagged | Pain 0–10 | Swelling | Likely factor), bullets on the top 2 patterns with the evidence and a confidence rating, steps for a flare-day plan (rest, ice or heat, pacing, medication as prescribed), and a callout on a joint that is hot, red and very painful, or fever with joint pain, needing same-day care.

tools.title: Low-impact plan
tools.subtitle: 4 weeks, joints included
tools.prompt: A 4-week {type} programme aiming for '{goal}' for the profile. Table (Week | Sessions | Duration | Strength moves | Progression), steps with form cues for the 3 key strengthening moves for the affected joints, bullets on the 2-hour pain rule and pacing, and a callout on stopping for sharp pain, swelling that lasts overnight, or chest symptoms.

tools.title: Tough-day pacing
tools.subtitle: Cold, wet, long hours on your feet

inputs.label: Tomorrow
inputs.placeholder: cold and wet, 6 hours on my feet at the market, then driving 2h

tools.prompt: Plan tomorrow: {day} with {energy} energy. Table (Time | Activity | Joint-saving adjustment | Rest micro-break), a checklist of what to wear and carry (layers, supports, grip aids, heat packs), bullets on car and standing ergonomics, and a callout on pacing so the day after is not lost.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Disease-modifying and pain medication decisions belong to your rheumatologist or GP. A single hot, red, very painful joint, or fever with joint pain, needs same-day medical care.
